title: Cohort Probing Decision Automaton for Canary/A-B Rollbacks
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Goal: Build a decision automaton that continuously probes user cohorts during canary and A/B rollouts, computes statistically robust quality deltas across a configurable metric set, and triggers automated, auditable rollback actions when pre-defined safety invariants are violated. The automaton must support multi-metric logic, hysteresis, minimum sample windows, and explainable provenance for why a rollback occurred.

Background: Current rollout guardrails rely on single-metric alerts and manual operator decisions. This leads to slow rollbacks or noisy false positives for ephemeral metric spikes. We need a reproducible system that: 1) evaluates per-cohort model behavior in production-like conditions, 2) aggregates signals with uncertainty estimates, 3) enforces rollback policies with cooldown and safe fallback operations, and 4) provides a clear audit trail (metrics, sample traces, causal precedence).

Design summary: The automaton runs in the rollout control plane and performs the following for each canary/A-B cohort window (default 5m):
- Collect request-level signals (latency, token_count, response_size) and evaluation signals (eval_hooks that compute quality metrics like prompt-specific exact_match, helpfulness_score, regression_rate on a seeded eval set plus sampled user prompts).
- Compute cohort-level metrics and confidence intervals using bootstrapped resampling and Bayesian A/B delta estimation. Store metric time series and CI in the rollout event log.
- Apply multi-metric decision rules (configurable ordered list) that combine absolute thresholds, relative deltas, and statistical significance. Example rule: if (preferred_quality_metric_delta <= -2.5% AND p_value < 0.01) OR (regression_rate_delta >= 0.7% AND sample_count >= 1000) then mark cohort as failing.
- Enforce hysteresis and cooldown: require failure in 3 consecutive windows OR persistent failure for >= 15 minutes before automated rollback. Emphasize quick operator-visible notification after first failing window.
- Automated rollback action: create rollback job that re-routes cohort traffic to the prior stable model variant, invalidates ephemeral caches where incompatible, triggers warmup path for fallback variant, and records the rollback event in audit logs + external ticket (e.g., JIRA/Linear link).

Key properties: explainability (store exemplars and top contributing prompts), repeatability (run offline replay to reproduce decision), safety (rate-limited rollback operations with leader election in control plane), and observability (per-cohort dashboard with metric deltas, CI bands, and sample traces).
acceptance_criteria: Automaton evaluates canary cohorts every 5 minutes and persists metrics to rollout event store
Decision rules support multi-metric boolean logic and configurable CI thresholds
Automated rollback is executed only after hysteresis rules and writes an auditable rollback event with sample traces and metric provenance
Rollbacks route traffic back to previous model variant and verify health before lifting the rollback state
Operator notifications (Slack + Console) fire on first failing window and on final automated rollback
Offline replay can reproduce the same decision given captured request stream and automaton config

risks_and_tradeoffs: False positives from noisy short windows: mitigated with hysteresis but increases time-to-rollback for real regressions
Sample bias across cohorts (VIP users vs. casual): we must weight cohorts and flag high-variance cohorts separately
Cost/latency of continuous eval hooks: minimize by using lightweight sampled evals and precomputed prompt buckets
Rollback complexity with model-compatibility (KV cache, quantization): require metadata to know safe fallback paths; otherwise fallback to full restart which is slower
Over-automation: need clear operator override and manual-approve mode for enterprise customers—default to safe auto for internal rollouts

testing_plan: Offline replay using last-month production request log to verify decision reproducibility
Shadow canary for 48 hours with automaton in 'observe' mode (no auto-rollback) to collect baseline false positive rate
Introduce synthetic regressions (15% quality delta on seeded prompts) to validate rollback triggers and timing
Chaos test: leader controller failover while an automated rollback is inflight
Post-rollback verification: run smoke eval on fallback variant and ensure traffic safety checks pass
monitoring_and_alerting: Per-cohort Grafana panels: metric delta, CI band, sample count, exemplar traces
Console notification: first-fail window (info), consensus-fail (warning), automated-rollback (critical)
SLO breach alert if rollback rate > 2 per 24h for same model family
Audit log retention 90 days for rollback events; exportable JSON with exemplars for postmortem
playbook_and_runbook: On first fail window: notify cohort owner + SRE, open provisional incident with automaton snapshot
On automated rollback: create Linear ticket, attach automaton decision provenance, kick off incident postmortem template
Manual override steps in Console: hold rollback, force promote candidate, or pin previous variant
Postmortem checklist: replay captured stream, reproduce metric delta, verify PR changes tied to rollout
